items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: we were with the Buck and Bubbles act for four and a half years. And we were never allowed to be away from Mr. Bubbles -- Nat Nazarrq.

ctx.x: Speaking of the cramp, Chuck, what would you say -- I mean it would take a student who would really have to be technically on top or what have you, to be able to do those cramp rolls and make them sound so -- look so easy, but we know it's not easy. How many years did that -- you know, did it take you tap dancing before you developed that style to be able to handle those cramps like that, like sort of falling off a log, for want of another expression?

Well, we were with the Buck and Bubbles act for four and a half years. And we were never allowed to be away from Mr. Bubbles -- Nat Nazarrq. We didn't stay with Mr. Buck because Mr. Buck had just his wife, you see. And three of those years, during three of those years, Mr. Bubbles, he trained Chuckles and I in tap dancing, what he called putting us through the paces. And he would make Chuckles and I dance a series of tempos, just to shape us up and make us stronger, because we were still growing lads, you see.…

used to take us around to the Rockland Palace, and he took us to a place on St. Nicholas Avenue called the Hotcha Club, and he took us to the Renaissance Ballroom, you know, and of course these was all wooden floors, and that's to keep us from getting anything like a hardening of the arteries. Most dancers used to be very afraid of getting hardening of the arteries. I don't see why, because they was -- in that kind of activity, I don't see why they could be getting any hardening of the arteries, because it…
